claims.claim: Library lending depends on borrowers having predictable access to loaned materials.
Libraries generally acquire rights that authorize them to lend ebooks.
Library ebook lending rights are often limited by time, price, or circulation conditions.
Libraries place licensed ebook titles in their catalogs and promise borrowers defined loan periods.
Publishers may legitimately withdraw ebook titles from future public-library loans.
Rights disputes sometimes cause publishers to withdraw ebook titles from library lending.
Digital library lending applications control ebook access through licensing controls and account authorization.
Digital library lending systems use the same access-control mechanisms both to enforce due dates and to revoke access immediately.
Immediate revocation of digital library ebook access can occur without conspicuous notice to the borrower.
Physical lending imposes constraints that make mid-loan seizure more difficult than revoking digital access.
Digital library checkout screens may be designed to resemble the experience of checking out material at a physical library desk.
Publisher contracts can require ebook titles to be withdrawn from new library circulation.
Libraries can update their catalogs in response to a publisher's withdrawal of a title.
Public libraries depend on public trust to perform their institutional role.
